free_tier.stated: Static routed /64 per tunnel, up to 5 tunnels per account, 100 Mbit/s per tunnel, dynamic IPv4 endpoint updates (dyndns2), self-service reverse DNS (PTR) - 0 kr / forever

egress.terms: no traffic allowance is stated for the free tunnel; 'Unlimited traffic' is listed on the paid VPN plan, not on the free tunnel plan; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: 'Copy the generated config - plain Linux, OpenWrt, or Windows. Standard 6in4, no client software'
tooling: four ip commands on Linux or a pasted router config; ddclient for the dyndns2 endpoint
chaining: needs a host with its own public IPv4, so it fits a free VM with an IPv4 address rather than one behind NAT.
binding_note: 100 Mbit/s is about thirty times the 3.24 Mbit/s that 1 TiB/month needs, and no byte quota is published, so nothing in the vocabulary fails at that volume. The real gate is protocol 41 reachability plus a public IPv4, and reachability is IPv6-only for the reader.

identity_cost.detail: 'Create an account at free.tunnel64.net and tell us the public IPv4 you connect from.' The paid VPN advertises 'Email-only signup - no name, no phone'; the free tunnel page states no field list.

reliability_note: 'Outbound port 25 is blocked by default' on the VPN side; the free tunnel plan publishes no SLA.
confidence_note: documented from the vendor page read today. No WireGuard on the free tier is the fact most worth re-checking, because the provider sells a WireGuard VPN next door.

evidence.proved: 'Static routed /64 per tunnel', 'Up to 5 tunnels per account', '100 Mbit/s per tunnel', '0 kr / forever'
'Standard 6in4, no client software, works on almost any router.'
'Sign up, tell us your public IPv4, and get a static point-to-point address plus a routed /64 for your whole LAN.'
a /48 plan is 'coming soon' and the VPN is a separate paid product

notes: Run on AS35100 from Sweden and the Philippines. A routed /48 tier is announced but not on sale. The free tier has no WireGuard, so a client that cannot receive protocol 41 gets nothing here; the paid VPN is the WireGuard path and it is priced, not free.

extras.wg_detail: the free tier is 6in4 only: 'Standard 6in4, no client software'. WireGuard exists on the paid VPN product ('WireGuard, on the same AS35100 hardware'), not on the free tunnel.
extras.volume_stated: no traffic allowance is stated for the free tunnel; 'Unlimited traffic' is listed on the paid VPN plan, not on the free tunnel plan
extras.transit_note: AS35100 terminates the tunnel on hardware the operator says it runs itself.
